bet.text: The fastest, shortest coral cycles that are hard to defend, from a ground intake and the lightest, fastest arm and elevator possible, with every motor kept low.

demand.text: Coral came first, without over-compromising on algae. It wanted to be sure of the climb, for its 12 points and the ranking point.
At the championship it expected division seeding to come down to tie breakers, so it took the co-op bonus whenever it could and seeded first on it alone.

auto.text: No planned paths: the team picks a start, a feeder and allowed branches, and the robot finds coral by camera and takes the closest branch.
The team's average was 4.73 pieces in auto at Johnson and 4.83 on Einstein.
At its district championship five pieces worked in 4 of 16 matches; in most it did not see the lollipop coral.

cycle.text: The driver steers toward a coral with assistance and the robot takes it in. The arm picks it from the conveyor and goes to placing position. When the driver allows, the robot curves to the nearest face and places at the highest allowed free level.
Its average: 17.47 pieces a match at ISR 1, 30.13 at Johnson.

endgame.text: Two tubes latch the cage with a magnet and centering prints, and a ratcheted winch climbs. Pressed with three seconds or less left, the climb runs at double acceleration and velocity, avoided otherwise because of the forces.

fallback.text: When a false sensor reading stuck the intake closed at ISR 1, the robot played only algae cycles and once took one from the ground, which it was not designed for. The operator could have overridden the sensor on the dashboard.
Against defense a dashboard toggle keeps the arm from going to place by itself.

gave_up.text: It was not designed for algae from the floor; in Einstein final 2 an opponent took its lollipop algae that way.
The elevator belt's spliced joint broke before ISR 1 and again before its district championship; a hot-welded replacement began failing at ISR 1, and a seam began to tear during Einstein.
Climber plates thinned to 4 mm for weight bent.

changed.text: The intake first tried to orient coral and jammed at steep angles, so a V indexer took over; after ISR 3 the front roller became all stars.
At ISR 1 the climber got 6 mm plates, aluminum rings and rubber tires, and a zip-tie failure point that snapped by itself was dropped.
Wide wedges later stopped the cage slipping out.

outcome.text: 62-9-0 in official play; won the Johnson division; championship finalist; captain of the Johnson alliance on Einstein; ranked 8 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 110.15, Johnson).

facts.text: Free speed
Four Kraken X60 drive motors and four Falcon steering motors
Same modules as 2024, regeared for acceleration over top speed because cycles are short

functions.name: Weight distribution

solves.text: Keep the center of gravity low with a tall elevator

functions.type: maximum frame perimeter with motors low

facts.text: The team says it can drive at full speed with elevator and arm fully extended without tipping
The highest motor, on the intake, sits at about
Custom bearing hubs weigh about half as much as off-the-shelf ones and also carry the elevator pulleys
During build 3 kg had to be found across the entire robot

solves.text: Take coral in any orientation, near a wall, the reef or a defender

facts.text: Plates of 1/4 in polycarbonate with brass bushings; the linkage collapses inward on impact and the plates flex in side hits
A slot lets the top roller slide up for vertical coral
Star compliant wheels replaced round ones because they give the most flexibility for the least space
A third roller was added at the back to fix a dead spot found on the robot

The four-bar collapses when both bar ends sit higher than their axes of rotation and the contact point is in line with or below the end of one bar (the post's picture marks which), so it moves only backward; friction and flex mean exaggerating this and using current limits
After ISR 3, a lighter all-star front roller picked up standing coral more consistently and let the lower roller be a thicker, softer rubber

cost.text: The intake and suction cup were the main development focus for most of the season
At ISR 3 the competition intake did noticeably worse than the practice one: a soft limit set slightly high left it floating instead of held down by the motor
Taking in two coral by accident was a bit of an issue; in teleop the driver can run the intake out by hand

solves.text: Center the coral on the robot every time

facts.text: Two sets of wheels in a V center the coral on the robot
Two Kraken X44 motors, so each side can be driven separately if a coral gets stuck
Comes off with four screws because the motors below drive it through hex shaft and printed couplers
Chosen over horizontal rollers pushing the coral into a wall

cost.text: Coral rebounding off the back wall could catch on the top plate and load the elevator until it skipped; a hole was cut in the plate after ISR 3

functions.name: Differential elevator and arm

solves.text: Move elevator and arm with no motors or gearboxes on the parts that go up

functions.type: three-stage differential elevator and arm on one belt loop

facts.text: Driven by two Kraken X60 motors at the bottom; moving both sides of the belt together lifts, a difference rotates the arm
Continuous HTD belt loop length
The arm is one carbon fiber tube with printed parts
Each motor's acceleration and top speed are changed during the move so the two motions stay in step and neither overshoots
The splice: about 8 cm of rubber is peeled from each end of an HTD belt to bare its Kevlar cords, which are bonded with DP604NS epoxy in an aluminum jig shaped like the teeth

Spliced because no belt of the wanted material came in the right length; a custom closed belt made for larger pulleys cracked, and the team strongly does not recommend splicing unless nothing else is viable
After ISR 3 gears replaced the 1:4 motor transmission belts, which skipped whatever their tension; with the indexer plate fix this allowed higher acceleration and jerk limits

Rollers to stop the big belt skipping were designed but, after ISR 3, not fitted, since a skip in an impact is better than a broken end effector; at the district championship the belt skipped when the arm hit a coral, not in normal use

Only an air tube runs up the elevator. The arm's absolute encoder, which the team planned to wire in March, was still unwired at the championship, because elevator and arm need a shared zeroing routine anyway
A slotted pulley mount, held by the friction of screws in M5 threaded inserts, tensions the belt

cost.text: The belt broke or began to fail on several occasions: a splice before ISR 1 and another before the district championship, a heat-welded polyurethane belt at ISR 1, and a splice that began to tear on Einstein; the team also counts two replacements for visible wear
An untested move from L4 to L3 exceeded acceleration limits and skipped an untensioned belt in the elevator transmission
The long arm puts large sideways forces on the elevator, which loosened things up and needed support in several directions

functions.name: Suction cup

solves.text: Hold coral and algae without a motor on the arm

functions.type: vacuum end effector for both pieces

facts.text: An off-the-shelf cup for coral inside a silicone seal for algae
The seal is molded in the shop in about a day, so it could be iterated quickly
Carriage, arm and manipulator together weigh about
A valve opens to release the piece
Only the inner cup is connected to vacuum; it seals on coral but lets air through on algae, where the outer seal holds. The team cleaned it before every match
The seal is Sorta-Clear silicone poured in a 3D printed mold
The release valve and vacuum sensor sit at the bottom of the elevator, so no electronics ride on it
Time from coral reaching the conveyor sensor to enough vacuum to move, early in the season; about 160 ms later
Two small dents on opposite sides of the end effector hold the preloaded coral at the start of auto

cost.text: It dropped one algae at the championship, in Einstein final 3
At ISR 3 algae dropped several times because going from floor coral straight to algae kept the coral's lower vacuum setting

At the district championship algae missed the net: the drop lagged the valve by a varying time and the release angle was shallow. Stopping before release was more consistent but much slower; 2.44 algae a match at 78%

functions.name: Vacuum pump

solves.text: Make steady vacuum at the base of the robot

functions.type: two pneumatic pistons driven by a Scotch yoke

facts.text: A motor at the base drives both pistons out of step, because one could not hold constant suction; the interview says half a cycle apart, a later team post a 90 degree offset
A vacuum sensor shows whether a piece is held; algae is held at more vacuum than coral
The pistons speed up on a leak and stop when vacuum holds, to save energy and wear
Vacuum reaches the end effector through 1/4 in tubing
Each piston pulls vacuum on both strokes, with two one-way valves at each end
Larger cylinders with more reduction, because a smaller bore had to pump so fast that it overheated; no cylinder was ever replaced
A Scotch yoke has the fewest moving parts and suited the limited space, and similar pistons were on hand for prototypes; it gave no issues

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Align to the cage quickly and stay up after the match

functions.type: two-tube cage latch with ratcheted winch

facts.text: Two aluminum tubes with centering prints and a magnet latch onto the cage
Climb rate by the team's count: 64.7% at ISR 1, 76.4% at ISR 3, 75% at the district championship, 100% at Johnson and Einstein
Distance between the two tubes; both got the rings and rubber tires

cost.text: At ISR 1 tape slipped on the official cages, tilting the robot into the chain; separately, bent 4 mm plates made it fall while climbing
At ISR 3 the swinging arm base bumped the chain, which referees ruled against, so the climb position moved the arm below the cage
At the district championship it lost a ranking point when its swing touched the carpet at the 3 second mark

solves.text: Place precisely on a target with little room for error

facts.text: Two Limelight 3G see the reef tags until the end of placing
A Limelight 3 on the other side, over the intake, also gives a precise location

MegaTag 1 for reef tags, merged by the team's simplified Kalman filter; its own angle-based calculation, used for barge and processor tags, depended too much on angle accuracy with this year's small height difference
Odometry's weight falls as the robot drives, to account for drift, and each module's path between loops is treated as an arc

solves.text: Help the driver line up with coral and collect it in auto

facts.text: A camera on an Orange Pi 5 with PhotonVision finds coral because nothing else on the floor is white
In teleop the assist acts across the robot's velocity and slows the driver when approaching fast; in auto the robot drives to the coral
The assist acts only when the coral is in the intake's view, the driver heads toward it, it can be reached soon and the robot is not turning fast, so that drivers do not notice it
After the district championship the team was making the lollipop coral a default target in auto, after a missed or undetected pickup or after the fourth piece

solves.text: Let the driver choose only the reef face

facts.text: The robot remembers where it placed, the operator adds what other teams did, and it picks the nearest face and highest allowed free level
It drives to a point short of the target in a smooth curve, then straight in

The curve keeps a nearly constant radius to a point short of the target, so the cameras face the tag for the final drive; a Bezier curve did not pass through that point, 0.5 m short. Limits are 4.3 m/s and 9 m/s2
L1 has three places per face; after three coral there it takes the nearest, and the driver can switch by flicking the stick

functions.name: Designed failure point

solves.text: Protect the arm from big impacts

functions.type: zip-tied joint meant to break in an arm impact

facts.text: It saved the robot from several catastrophic failures in testing
The permanent fix was one piece of tube

cost.text: A zip tie snapped by itself in one match and the joint did not fail when needed in another

decisions.choice: Vacuum for both coral and algae
decisions.because: it keeps the arm and manipulator as light as possible
motors and gearboxes stay at the bottom
decisions.cost: a belt that broke or began to fail on several occasions

decisions.choice: Let the intake accept coral any way round and orient it in a separate indexer
decisions.because: an intake that oriented coral got stuck at steep angles and was only marginally faster than driving to the station
decisions.instead_of: an intake that does the orienting

decisions.because: it orients coral and is much better at centering it

decisions.choice: Two vacuum pistons out of step
decisions.because: one piston could not create constant suction
the robot goes to the closest branch instead of a set one, which saves time
not having to fight through defense for every piece mattered, seen in a match with a dedicated defender

decisions.choice: Limit the third robot to loading-station cycles in one lane
decisions.because: it stopped getting in the way of the two ground-pickup scorers and output improved dramatically
decisions.instead_of: sending it for algae and opponent coral, or to defend

decisions.choice: Plan each prototype around a test
decisions.because: prototypes built poorly or without anything to prove wasted a lot of time

decisions.choice: Belt instead of a capstan on the differential elevator
decisions.because: rope creeping along a capstan changes the path length a little, tolerable on a regular elevator but possibly noticeable slop in the arm

decisions.choice: Cylinder pump built by the team
decisions.because: the small pumps it tried in the 2021 off-season had poor suction for their noise and energy use

decisions.choice: Score wherever is closest, whatever the level
decisions.because: at the district championship strong partners would fill most of L3 and L4 anyway, and two coral on the near L1 are usually faster than one L2 or L3 on the far side

decisions.choice: Pick a floor-coral partner at the district championship
decisions.because: the loading-station robot struggled against defense and the floor-coral one seemed unfazed
decisions.instead_of: a partner that climbed and took algae from the floor

decisions.choice: Keep prototyping the floor intake after three days without success
decisions.because: the team expected it to shorten cycles, and the concept was kept able to fit a wide hopper if it failed

decisions.choice: One driver controls all robot states
decisions.because: relying little on talk between driver and commander prevents miscommunication; the commander only sets the top level and marks others' placements
